quote.text: Travel is fatal to prejudice, bigotry, and narrow-mindedness, and many of our people need it sorely on these accounts.
quote.author: Mark Twain, The Innocents Abroad, 1869

stories.headline: Beni Rugs prints its knot counts and its prices; Jan Kath prints neither
stories.dek: A London house charges US$220 a square foot for a rug knotted in Kathmandu. The category’s central fraud is not the wool — it is the phrase “hand-knotted”, and you settle it by turning the rug over.

stories.headline: Practical Machinist carries 3.2 million posts; Model Engineer has published since 1898
stories.dek: Hobby metalworking runs on two machines and some very large communities: 59,994 members on The Hobby-Machinist, 1.1 million on the metalworking subreddit. The hook is never the machine — it is the first part you cut to a number and it fits.

stories.kicker: The Travel Desk · Japan’s Tax-Free Switch
stories.headline: Tax-free shopping in Japan ends on 1 November; you will claim at the airport
stories.dek: Purchases up to 31 October follow the old National Tax Agency rules. From Sunday week the minimum spend is ¥5,000 regardless of goods type, and the sealed-bag rule and the ¥500,000 daily cap both go.

stories.headline: PHP patched two AI-found remote-code flaws; Finland and Japan took sites offline
stories.dek: The security firm Calif found the pair on 1 August using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. Patches shipped at 14:00 UTC on 21 October, and Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency issued its own alert the same day.

stories.headline: Home prices rose 1.4 per cent as URA put vacancy at 7.2 per cent
stories.dek: The Urban Redevelopment Authority’s full third-quarter statistics, out on 23 October, confirm the flash estimate exactly. Developers launched 1,140 units and sold 1,183, both sharply down; 32,800 unsold homes could reach the market inside two years.

stories.headline: Nscale’s IPO filing carries Anthropic’s GPU order with every number blacked out
stories.dek: The British cloud firm attached the contract to its 18 September S-1. Anthropic holds a written veto over what Nscale may show the Securities and Exchange Commission — and Anthropic itself still has no filing of its own on EDGAR.

stories.headline: Sigma’s fp2 arrives at US$2,199 with no mechanical shutter and no stabilisation
stories.dek: Announced on 23 October and shipping 11 November from Aizu, the 24.5-megapixel body is the smallest full-frame camera made. Flash sync is capped at 1/50s, and the grip and finder take the working price to US$2,982.

stories.headline: Audio-Technica priced the ATH-AWX7000 at US$3,799 and published no measurements
stories.dek: On sale from 23 October: Kiso cypress earcups in Echizen lacquer, deerskin pads, a new 58-millimetre composite diaphragm. The release gives no impedance, no sensitivity, no frequency response and no weight.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · Klara And The Sun
stories.headline: Taika Waititi’s Ishiguro adaptation opened on 23 October to 23 per cent
stories.dek: Columbia put Klara and the Sun into wide release with Jenna Ortega as the solar-powered narrator. Rotten Tomatoes has it at 23 per cent on 60 reviews and Metacritic at 30 from 24 critics; the audience score is withheld for want of ratings.

stories.headline: JAMA Pediatrics finds one in six US adolescents reporting moderate or severe anxiety
stories.dek: An analysis of 15,730 twelve-to-twenty-year-olds, published by Bommersbach on 12 October, puts severe symptoms at 7.2 per cent — and 41.2 per cent of that group had no mental-health treatment at all in the preceding year.

stories.kicker: Fitness · The Ring On The Bench
stories.headline: NUS validated the Oura ring against actigraphy on 41 adults aged twenty-six
stories.dek: Sleep Health published the comparison on 9 October: agreement of 0.67 to 0.98 across rest-activity metrics. Three of the six authors sit in the Oura–NUS Joint Lab, and a mid-forties reader is twenty years older than the sample.

stories.kicker: The Diary · Before The Year Turns
stories.headline: ART SG’s two-for-one tickets expire on 24 November; sumo opens 5 December
stories.dek: BABYMONSTER’s two Indoor Stadium nights on 28 and 29 November are the only big show with a published price ladder, S$168 to S$358. Nothing else checked carries a sold-out flag.

stories.headline: Nine state-owned Guangxi power retailers warned the regional government of mass bankruptcies
stories.dek: The petition went in on 30 September from subsidiaries holding about 70 per cent of the regional market. The trade’s phrase for what is happening is 批零倒挂 — wholesale and retail hanging upside down — and Guangxi’s retailers expect to lose more than five billion yuan this year.
